title: Power Mean Estimation in Stochastic Continuous Monte Carlo Tree Search
abstract: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) has demonstrated success in online planning for deterministic environments, yet significant challenges remain in adapting it to stochastic Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), particularly in continuous state-action spaces. Existing methods, such as HOOT, which combines MCTS with the Hierarchical Optimistic Optimization (HOO) bandit strategy, address continuous spaces but rely on a logarithmic exploration bonus that lacks theoretical guarantees in non-stationary, stochastic settings. Recent advancements, such as POLY-HOOT, introduced a polynomial bonus term to achieve convergence in deterministic MDPs, though a similar theory for stochastic MDPs remains undeveloped. In this paper, we propose a novel MCTS algorithm, \Algname, designed for continuous, stochastic MDPs. \Algname integrates a power mean as a value backup operator, alongside a polynomial exploration bonus to address the non-stationarity inherent in continuous action spaces. Our theoretical analysis establishes that \Algname converges at a polynomial rate of $\mathcal{O}(n^{-ζ})$, $ζ\in (0,1/2)$, where \( n \) is the number of visited trajectories, thereby extending the non-asymptotic convergence guarantees of POLY-HOOT to stochastic environments. Experimental results on stochastic tasks validate our theoretical findings, demonstrating the effectiveness of \Algname in continuous, stochastic domains.

title: Disparity Has a Sign: Stereo Matching Beyond the Zero-Disparity Plane
abstract: Modern stereo matching models fail when disparity crosses zero, with end-point error (EPE) rising by 4.6-37$\times$. Yet stereoscopic content, from cinema 3D to VR, routinely contains objects behind the zero-disparity plane (ZDP), corresponding to negative disparities. The blind spot cascades through datasets, architectures, and evaluation protocols, all of which inherit the non-negative geometry. Rectified parallel cameras place ZDP at infinity, so every finite depth yields $d=fB/z \ge 0$ by construction, and nothing within the standard pipeline can violate, or even measure, a negative disparity. To measure it, we propose \textit{ZDPShift}, a benchmark of $21{,}495$ stereo pairs from seven cinematographer-authored open movies, each frame rendered at five zero-disparity-plane positions with dense signed ground truth. Six state-of-the-art image and video stereo matching models collapse once the plane moves. On identical scene content, FoundationStereo goes from $2.24$ px EPE to $75.33$px, with every backbone leaving roughly half of all pixels exceeding a three-pixel disparity error. What is missing, however, is not the underlying matching capability. % The capability itself, however, is already present. Training on supervision synthesized from SceneFlow, which adds no new data or parameters, keeps the error flat across the signed range. Training only the decoder, with the pretrained matching features frozen, performs comparably across all six backbones, with EPE jittering within $0.2$px. Thus, the pretrained features already extend to the negative regime they were never trained on, and only the output convention discarded it. Meanwhile, positive-regime accuracy on KITTI, Middlebury, ETH3D, and Sintel is largely preserved.

title: Decomposing LLM-Judge Uncertainty to Target Expert Labels
abstract: An LLM judge evaluates outputs at scale. Experts should label only where it is least sure. Its natural escalation signal conflates two uncertainties: aleatoric, real disagreement in the expert pool, which labels cannot reduce, and epistemic, the judge's ignorance, which labels do reduce. A small Bayesian model separates them: a regression on labels already collected learns how far to trust a black-box judge's prediction. Both components follow as simple formulas, with no sampling or further judge calls. The components isolate on a real LLM judge against exactly known truth, and stated confidence is no guide to its actual error. On real human disagreement (ChaosNLI) the epistemic ranking removes 83% more error than total uncertainty for the same expert labels, though simply escalating the least-labelled items does as well there. We demonstrate we can estimate where a judge is ignorant rather than where experts genuinely disagree, and propose using this to direct expert labelling. Code and data are available at https://github.com/composo-ai/judge-uncertainty-decomposition.

title: Quantum Exposure Assessment of Public-Sector TLS Infrastructure Using a Composite Cryptographic Index
abstract: Purpose – This study develops and empirically evaluates a Quantum Exposure Index (QEI) for characterizing quantum-related exposure observable from public-sector Transport Layer Security (TLS) infrastructures and supporting post-quantum migration prioritization. Methods – The framework integrates TLS protocol version, certificate public-key algorithm, classical key-strength equivalence, and Perfect Forward Secrecy into a normalized composite index. Component weights were derived through the Analytical Hierarchy Process, while non-intrusive TLS measurements from publicly accessible government infrastructures provided the empirical inputs. Sensitivity and sector-level analyses were conducted to examine the robustness and interpretability of the resulting exposure profiles. Findings – The evaluated infrastructures remain dependent on classical public-key cryptography and therefore retain exposure to future quantum-capable adversaries despite widespread adoption of modern TLS configurations and forward secrecy. The analysis further shows that cryptographic key strength and protocol configuration differentiate exposure profiles, whereas the continued reliance on quantum-vulnerable public-key primitives establishes a common exposure baseline. Classification outcomes are sensitive to interpretive thresholds, reinforcing the importance of continuous index values over categorical labels. Research Implications – The QEI provides a reproducible infrastructure-level baseline for prioritizing cryptographic inventories, monitoring migration progress, and supporting evidence-based post-quantum transition planning. Originality – This study combines operational TLS measurement, standardized cryptographic-strength mapping, and multicriteria weighting within a unified quantitative framework for assessing observable quantum exposure in public-sector infrastructures.

title: AbyssGeist "探渊索隐"——地学AI大模型策划案
abstract: AbyssGeist “探渊索隐” is a conceptual proposal for an AI foundation model oriented toward geophysics, geology, mineral exploration, and the mining industry. 本策划案提出以多模态地球物理数据、地质先验知识图谱与历史数据相似性检索为基础,探索地学人工智能在物探资料解释、异常识别、成矿预测及矿产资源勘查中的应用路径,并进一步构想从勘探、钻探、采选冶到资源贸易的数字化反馈闭环。本方案献礼矿大115周年校庆 本作品为概念性策划与技术架构白皮书,并不代表 AbyssGeist 大模型已经完成开发或部署。

title: Probability Logic Networks: Adaptive Learning Mechanisms
abstract: Probability Logic Networks (PLN) represent a powerful framework for learning complex patterns from data. Traditional implementations often rely on static network configurations, limiting their ability to adapt to evolving data and improving model generalization. This paper introduces a novel adaptive learning mechanism for PLN, leveraging reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust network structure and weights. The core principle is to train the network through feedback on input data, allowing it to adapt to the specific characteristics of the dataset. This approach significantly enhances feature extraction and improves model robustness. We present a detailed explanation of the mechanism, its implementation, and experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: 基于自适应的量子计算的量子态跃迁算法
abstract: This paper explores the application of a novel adaptive quantum computing algorithm, designed to enhance quantum state transition rates. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their computational efficiency. We present a new approach that dynamically adjusts quantum state transition parameters to optimize the execution of quantum algorithms. This optimization is achieved through a feedback mechanism that continuously evaluates and refines the transition probabilities, leading to significantly improved efficiency in quantum state manipulation. The core of this algorithm is a sophisticated feedback loop that adapts to the inherent dynamics of the quantum system, resulting in enhanced performance compared to existing methods. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive approach through simulations and preliminary experimental results, illustrating its potential to revolutionize quantum computation.

title: 基于自适应量子态的拓扑信息编码
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging adaptive quantum states for information encoding, presenting a novel quantum state encoding scheme. The core concept revolves around utilizing the dynamic nature of quantum states to achieve efficient and secure information transmission. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the quantum state based on the encoded information, optimizing for both compression and information security. This approach aims to overcome limitations of traditional quantum information encoding methods and opens avenues for advanced quantum communication protocols. The proposed system demonstrates the potential for enhanced information transfer and security through the integration of adaptive quantum states.

title: 基于量子算法的复杂系统模拟
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum algorithms to accelerate the simulation of complex systems. Complex systems, characterized by intricate interactions and emergent properties, pose significant computational challenges for traditional simulation methods. We propose a novel framework leveraging quantum computation to overcome these limitations, utilizing quantum algorithms to efficiently represent and evolve complex systems. The core mechanism focuses on employing quantum approximation algorithms to reduce the computational cost of simulations, thereby enabling the study of systems with vast complexity. The paper details the design of the quantum simulation framework, including the selection of appropriate quantum algorithms and the implementation of a simulation pipeline. The potential benefits of this approach include significantly reduced simulation times, the ability to model systems with higher fidelity, and the potential for uncovering novel insights into the dynamics of complex phenomena. This research investigates the feasibility and performance of this framework, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulated examples and preliminary analysis.

We propose a novel framework leveraging quantum computation to overcome these limitations, utilizing quantum algorithms to efficiently represent and evolve complex systems. title: Title: Dynamic Parameter Adjustment Framework for Topological Genetic Algorithms (DGP)
abstract: The stability and performance of machine learning models are crucial for various applications. However, traditional machine learning algorithms often rely on static parameters, which can lead to suboptimal results and a lack of generalization ability. This paper introduces the Dynamic Parameter Adjustment Framework (DGP) – a novel approach to optimize machine learning models through dynamic parameter adjustments. DGP leverages a dynamically adjusted parameter set to guide the optimization process, resulting in improved model performance and enhanced generalization. This work explores the potential of dynamically adjusting model parameters to overcome limitations of static model optimization techniques.

title: Quantum-Guided Optimization for Non-Linear Differential Equations
abstract: Quantum-Guided Optimization (QGO) offers a promising approach to solving complex nonlinear differential equations, particularly those exhibiting significant curvature. This paper investigates the potential of quantum tunneling to accelerate the optimization process, addressing the limitations of classical methods in such scenarios. We present a novel QGO framework utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to enhance the exploration of the solution space, demonstrating improved convergence speed and resilience to local minima compared to traditional optimization techniques. The core mechanism centers on leveraging quantum tunneling to facilitate a more efficient search, ultimately leading to faster and more robust solutions. The research explores the practical implications of this approach, focusing on the design of a quantum algorithm tailored for this specific problem.

title: Hierarchical Memory Networks for Multi-Scale Data Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to multi-scale data analysis utilizing Hierarchical Memory Networks (HMNs). Traditional Memory Networks (MemNets) often face challenges when dealing with data exhibiting vastly different scales of dependencies. The proposed framework addresses this limitation through a multi-level hierarchical architecture. Each level of the hierarchy employs a Memory Network specifically designed to process data at its corresponding scale and abstraction level. Inter-level communication is established using learned attention mechanisms, enabling effective reasoning across these diverse scales. The core claim is that this architecture significantly improves the ability to capture and analyze data with complex, multi-scale dependencies. The key mechanism involves the layered design and learned attention, offering a robust framework for integration and reasoning across varying data scales, ultimately enhancing performance on complex problems. Mathematical notation and formulas are presented in plain text for compatibility.

title: Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Gradient Descent with Entangled Parameter Updates
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to stochastic gradient descent (SGD) inspired by quantum entanglement. The core idea is that parameter updates in a neural network can be significantly accelerated by leveraging correlations between parameters, mimicking the behavior of entangled quantum systems. We introduce a shared tensor network representing a quantum state amongst the network's parameters. Parameter updates are then performed by manipulating this shared state, effectively creating an entangled state that reduces the variance of the gradient estimate. This approach, termed Quantum-Inspired SGD with Entangled Parameter Updates (QISGD-EPU), offers a potential pathway to dramatically improve the training speed of deep neural networks. Theoretical analysis suggests that the correlation inherent in the shared state can lead to faster convergence and reduced sensitivity to the learning rate. We outline the mathematical framework, the update rules, and discuss the potential benefits and challenges of this new paradigm.

title: Quantum-Inspired Algorithms for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper explores the development and application of novel optimization algorithms inspired by the principles of quantum mechanics. Recognizing the potential of quantum phenomena like superposition and tunneling for enhancing computational efficiency, we propose a new algorithmic framework that mimics these behaviors within a classical computing environment. The core idea is to construct an optimization algorithm that incorporates probabilistic search strategies, analogous to quantum tunneling, and explores multiple solution possibilities concurrently, similar to superposition. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional optimization methods, particularly in tackling complex, high-dimensional problems. We detail the algorithm's design, emphasizing the key mathematical formulations and probabilistic elements. The proposed algorithm's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual demonstrations, showcasing its potential to offer improved convergence rates and solution quality compared to established classical optimization techniques. The research contributes to the burgeoning field of quantum-inspired computing, providing a practical and accessible approach for leveraging quantum concepts for optimization challenges.

title: Title: Quantum Simulation of Non-Markovian Processes via Entangled Observables
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented capabilities for modeling complex systems, particularly those exhibiting non-Markovian dynamics. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent complexities of non-Markovian systems, requiring significant computational resources and potentially inaccurate results. This paper proposes a novel quantum simulation technique centered around the entanglement of observables, aiming to overcome these limitations by embracing a fundamentally different approach to system dynamics. The core claim is to develop a quantum simulation method capable of accurately modeling non-Markovian processes by leveraging the enhanced power of entangled observations. We detail the mechanism, explore the theoretical framework, and present initial experimental explorations demonstrating the technique's potential for improved fidelity in simulating complex quantum systems.

title: Topological Embedding-based Neural Network Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network learning based on topological embedding. The core idea is to leverage the inherent topological structure of neural networks to guide the learning process, ultimately enhancing the network's generalization ability and robustness. We introduce the concept of a "topological embedding space," where a neural network is mapped to a lower-dimensional space based on its connectivity. Learning within this space utilizes the geometric information captured by the embedding, leading to improved network performance. Unlike conventional methods that primarily rely on local information, our approach incorporates global network topology, addressing a significant limitation in current neural network learning paradigms. We explore the theoretical foundations and potential benefits of this methodology, highlighting its capacity to improve learning efficiency and network resilience.

title: Evolutionary Algorithm-Driven Compiler Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to compiler optimization utilizing evolutionary algorithms. Traditional compiler optimization relies on static, hand-crafted rules, often failing to adapt effectively to diverse hardware architectures and application-specific needs. We introduce a framework where compiler optimization rules are represented as individuals within a population, subject to evolution through a genetic algorithm. The algorithm iteratively refines these rules, selecting those that yield the best performance based on a defined fitness function. This dynamic optimization process overcomes the limitations of static rules, offering the potential for significantly improved code efficiency. The core claim is that applying evolutionary algorithms to compiler optimization can lead to solutions tailored to specific environments. The mechanism involves treating optimization rules as individuals within a population and using a genetic algorithm to evolve them. The research addresses the need for adaptable optimization strategies in a wide range of computing environments. We demonstrate, theoretically, the potential advantages of this approach and outline a roadmap for future development and implementation.

title: Universal Quantum State Representations
abstract: Quantum state representation is a fundamental aspect of quantum information theory, crucial for quantum computation and quantum communication. Current approaches often struggle with representing and manipulating quantum states across multiple dimensions and quantum dimensions. This paper proposes a novel framework for representing and manipulating quantum states, centered around the concept of a 'multi-dimensional state space' metric, which allows for the translation of quantum states across multiple scales. This framework aims to overcome limitations of existing methods and pave the way for universal quantum state representations.

title: Chaos-Driven Adaptive Algorithm Generation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to algorithm generation by leveraging the inherent properties of chaotic systems. The core idea is to utilize the sensitivity of chaotic systems to initial conditions – the "butterfly effect" – to automatically generate and optimize algorithms for various problems. The methodology involves controlling the parameters of a chaotic system, observing its output, and then extracting algorithmic structure and rules based on the observed characteristics. This process allows for the creation of algorithms tailored to specific problem domains without relying on traditional, human-designed approaches. The generated algorithms are then evaluated based on their performance and adaptability. This work demonstrates the potential of chaotic systems as dynamic generators of algorithms, offering a fundamentally different perspective on algorithm design and optimization. The key mathematical concepts explored include the logistic map, Lyapunov exponents, and fractal dimensions, all central to characterizing and controlling chaotic systems. The resulting algorithms are not merely approximations of existing solutions but rather novel structures born from the unpredictable behavior of the underlying chaotic system. This approach holds promise for tackling complex and evolving problems where adaptability and robustness are paramount.

title: MARR: Decoupling Policy, Execution, and Calibration for All-in-One Medical Image Restoration
abstract: All-in-one medical image restoration seeks to recover heterogeneous clinical images with a single model, but PET, CT, and MRI differ substantially in degradation statistics, anatomical contrast, and output-space bias. A fully shared network can entangle modality-specific residual errors, whereas separate modality-specific networks sacrifice the practical advantages of unified deployment. We therefore recast all-in-one restoration as a question of where limited adaptation should be placed: policy selection, feature execution, or output calibration. We propose MARR, a compact restoration framework that constrains multi-modality adaptation into degradation-aware policy routing, modality-private residual execution, and image-domain residual correction without requiring degradation labels or separate modality-specific models. The policy branch forms a routing prompt from input statistics, latent content, and modality identity, and uses it only as a control signal. Prompt-gated modality-private adapters then perform lightweight residual refinement at intermediate decoder stages, while zero-initialized modality-specific output heads calibrate the final image-domain residual without perturbing the initial shared prediction. On an all-in-one PET, CT, and MRI restoration benchmark, MARR outperforms thirteen methods re-trained under the same protocol, achieving PSNR values of 37.34 dB, 33.85 dB, and 32.09 dB on PET, CT, and MRI, respectively, and the best modality-average PSNR of 34.43 dB. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/CHB-learner/MARR.

title: Behavioral Cloning Outperforms Entropy-Regularized RL: Critic-Driven Failure of Actor-Critic Methods on Adaptive Tumor Treatment
abstract: Adaptive dosing requires policies that reduce tumor burden without excessive toxicity. Learned dosing policies are typically judged against historical or heuristic comparators, which cannot show whether a policy has found the best behavior available. We instead study a three-population tumor-control ODE in which optimal-control analysis fixes the form of a good schedule -- bang-bang dosing punctuated by a singular arc -- and construct a numerical controller of that form as a proxy for near-optimal behavior. Judged against this reference under a sustained-cure criterion -- 200 consecutive days below 5% carrying capacity -- Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) trained from scratch never reaches cure. Behavioral cloning (BC) of the reference reproduces it (100% sustained cure, 30/30 seeds), but SAC fine-tuning of the cloned policy destroys it across five entropy coefficients, and TD3 and BC-regularized SAC fail identically; the pattern persists under multiplicative pharmacokinetic action noise. Along curative trajectories the post-collapse critic ranks the collapsed-policy action above the reference action in 96% of states, concentrated in the maintenance phase, and the policy settles into a non-curative adaptive-therapy equilibrium. The reference is what makes this legible: against a heuristic comparator the fine-tuned policy would read as a competent controller rather than a failure.

title: Sector-Mean: Deterministic Initialization of K-Means Centroids via Angular Sector Partitioning
abstract: K-Means is one of the most widely used clustering algorithms, but its susceptibility to initial centroid selection remains a primary bottleneck for its convergence speed and clustering accuracy. This paper proposes Sector-Mean Initialization, a deterministic initialization strategy with O(N) time complexity that partitions the two-dimensional data space into angular sectors around the global centroid and initializes centroids using sector-wise means. We evaluate the method on established two-dimensional benchmarks (SIPU, Birch) and multiple real-world datasets, comparing against random, K-Means++, and Max-Min initialization under identical Lloyd iterations. The statistical analysis of Friedman's test (p<0.05) and Nemenyi post-hoc comparison indicates that, while delivering equivalent clustering quality as K-Means++ and Max-Min, Sector-Mean offers significant computational efficiency. Experimental results show that Sector-Mean reduces the initialization time by 74.9% and 59.8% in comparison to K-Means++ and max-min, respectively. And, it yields the lowest average number of iterations, achieving approximately 5% fewer iterations than K-Means++ and 16% fewer than max-min. These results highlight that Sector-Mean initialization offers a deterministic and computationally efficient initialization strategy while preserving cluster quality.

title: sofi-tabular: Sparseness Optimized Feature Importance
abstract: Sparseness Optimized Feature Importance (SOFI) is a model-agnostic, declarative post hoc explainer. An explanation takes the form of a ranking of features, and its quality is the degradation score obtained after cumulative marginalization. The implementation supports classification and regression, operates at the instance level or over a whole dataset, and marginalizes one-hot encoded features as indivisible blocks.

title: From Local Predictability to Long-Horizon Actionability
abstract: This systematic falsification study tests whether locally informative training-time signals can yield reliable long-horizon improvements in neural-network generalization. It evaluates adaptive interventions from feature-level reliability gating and counterfactual utility through pathway-gradient routing and example-level reweighting, using matched controls and predefined stage gates. Although several signals were measurable and locally predictive, no intervention produced replicated improvement over matched controls. The work therefore distinguishes local predictability and one-step causal benefit from long-horizon actionability, and documents the full experimental progression, invalidated runs, controls, and stopping criterion for a rigorous negative result.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Sampling of Complex Distributions
abstract: Quantum computing promises revolutionary advancements across numerous fields, and sampling from complex probability distributions is a critical step in many scientific and engineering disciplines. Traditional methods often struggle with the exponential growth of possibilities, limiting the computational efficiency of these tasks. This research proposes a novel quantum-enhanced sampling approach designed to overcome these limitations, utilizing quantum algorithms to efficiently explore the space of possible distributions. The core mechanism centers around leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement to accelerate the identification of key patterns and correlations within complex data, ultimately leading to improved representation and analysis of uncertain data. This paper details the theoretical framework, algorithm implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of this approach to significantly enhance distribution sampling.

title: Dynamically Adaptive Kernel Learning for Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has achieved remarkable success in various domains, yet its performance often degrades when facing non-stationary environments or complex reward structures. A key limitation lies in the reliance on fixed kernels within DRL architectures, particularly in Gaussian Processes (GPs) used for function approximation. These fixed kernels restrict the agent's ability to dynamically adapt to changes, hindering optimal learning. This paper proposes a Dynamically Adaptive Kernel Learning (DAKL) framework that addresses this issue. DAKL introduces a kernel learning module that continuously updates the kernel parameters using a Bayesian optimization strategy. This mechanism allows the kernel to evolve alongside the agent's experience, effectively creating a truly adaptive representation of the environment. The core claim is that fixed kernels in DRL limit adaptability. The core mechanism utilizes a Bayesian optimization framework to guide kernel parameter updates. The novelty lies in transitioning from static kernels to a continuously evolving representation, significantly improving DRL performance in dynamic settings.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Topological Feedback
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design centered around incorporating topological feedback loops to achieve inherent self-correction and robustness. Traditional neural network training focuses primarily on adjusting weights to minimize error, often leaving networks vulnerable to damage or disruption. We argue that a more fundamental solution lies in designing networks with explicitly defined topological constraints that actively maintain network connectivity and stability. This is achieved through the introduction of feedback loops that dynamically adjust network structure in response to detected anomalies. The core claim is that by leveraging topological feedback, neural networks can move beyond passive learning towards an active state of self-repair and adaptation. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, outlining key design considerations and illustrating how these feedback loops can mitigate the impact of node failures, connection disruptions, and other forms of network degradation. The presented framework represents a significant departure from conventional neural network design, offering a pathway to inherently robust and self-correcting systems. The proposed method relies on maintaining a degree of network connectivity and stability through the implementation of topological feedback loops.

title: Adversarial Robustness Certification via Formal Verification of Neural Network Layers
abstract: The vulnerability of neural networks to adversarial attacks poses a significant challenge to their deployment in safety-critical applications. While empirical methods for assessing robustness, such as adversarial training, have shown some success, they often lack rigorous guarantees about the level of protection offered. This paper proposes a novel approach to adversarial robustness certification by leveraging formal verification techniques applied directly to the layers of a neural network. We introduce a methodology that employs model checking to mathematically prove that a given layer's output remains within a specified region around its nominal output when perturbed by small adversarial inputs. This approach moves beyond black-box testing and provides a concrete, verifiable guarantee of robustness. The core claim is that the robustness of neural networks can be formally certified by verifying the robustness of individual layers. We outline the core mechanism of applying model checking to formally verify that a specific layer's output remains within a defined region around its nominal output when subjected to small, adversarial perturbations. This paper establishes a foundational framework for building more trustworthy and reliable neural networks. ---

title: ##基于神经符号推理的程序自动生成
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis leveraging the combined power of deep learning and neuro-symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to create a neuro-symbolic hybrid model where a deep learning component interprets program functionality and identifies patterns, while a neuro-symbolic component handles program logic representation and reasoning. An intermediate layer facilitates interaction between these two components, ultimately leading to the generation of program code. Unlike traditional automatic programming techniques that rely heavily on rule-based systems or templates, our method incorporates semantic understanding and reasoning, addressing a critical limitation in existing approaches. We demonstrate the potential of this synergistic approach to generate programs with specific functionalities and semantic meaning. The system is designed to learn from examples and then apply this knowledge to generate new, functionally equivalent programs. This work aims to bridge the gap between symbolic and sub-symbolic AI techniques, offering a more robust and flexible solution for automated program development. ---

title: Non-Balanced Reinforcement Learning with Policy Gradient Optimization
abstract: This paper addresses the challenges posed by non-balanced reinforcement learning environments. We introduce a novel policy gradient optimization algorithm designed to effectively learn optimal policies in such scenarios. The core of our approach lies in the estimation of state-action value functions, coupled with a robust exploration strategy that leverages sampling methods for policy gradient updates. Traditional policy gradient methods often struggle in non-balanced environments, frequently falling into local optima due to a lack of sufficient exploration. Our algorithm mitigates this issue by incorporating a dynamic exploration mechanism, leading to improved convergence and performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through theoretical analysis and provide a clear explanation of its components and their interactions. The goal is to provide a foundational approach for tackling complex, non-uniform reinforcement learning problems. ---

title: Seven-Word Subcore Exclusions and a Six-Hole Plateau in the Ternary Covering Problem K_3(7,3)
abstract: Technical report, software, and reproducible finite computations for scoped structural exclusions in the unresolved ternary covering-code problem K_3(7,3). For each of eight seven-word subcores obtained by deleting one word from an explicit eight-word core, every set of at most four added centers leaves at least six radius-3 holes, and equality is attained. Consequently, no size-at-most-11 covering code contains any of these subcores or an isometric copy. Independent Rust and C++20 implementations verify the four deletion-orbit representatives by exact pair reduction, building 9,500,440 pair entries and querying 347,365 eligible first pairs. The release also classifies the exact three-center completions of the eight-word core, an exact six-hole replacement plateau, and a diameter-at-most-4 lower bound of 17. The global interval 11 <= K_3(7,3) <= 12 remains unchanged.

title: Explainable AI for Automated Theorem Proving via Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: Automated theorem proving (ATP) systems have achieved remarkable success in verifying complex mathematical theorems. However, their opacity – the lack of human-understandable explanations for their reasoning – remains a significant barrier to widespread adoption. This research proposes a novel approach to enhance the explainability of ATP systems by integrating counterfactual reasoning. We leverage the "what if" scenario – exploring alternative possibilities – to provide transparent justifications for each step in the theorem proving process. This method identifies critical steps and generates counterfactual scenarios, allowing users to understand *why* a particular step was taken and to assess the robustness of the overall proof. The core claim is that integrating counterfactual analysis into ATP systems significantly improves transparency and trustworthiness, ultimately increasing their accessibility and utility. This paper details the framework, outlines the key components, and provides a conceptual overview of the approach, highlighting its potential impact on the field of automated reasoning.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Memory Access Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed memory access optimization leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core idea centers around establishing a network of entangled particles, each linked to a storage unit within a distributed memory system. Measurement of one entangled particle instantaneously reveals the state of its associated storage unit, circumventing traditional distance-based delays. We define the system as: Let $S = \{s_1, s_2, ..., s_K\}$ be the set of storage units in the distributed memory system. Let $E = \{e_1, e_2, ..., e_K\}$ be the set of entangled particles. Each $e_i$ is associated with a storage unit $s_i$, denoted as $e_i \leftrightarrow s_i$. The entanglement state of the system is denoted as $\rho = \sum_{i=1}^{K} p_i |e_i\rangle \langle e_i|$, where $p_i$ is the probability amplitude of the $i$-th entangled particle being in its state. Measuring the state of $e_i$ instantaneously determines the state of $s_i$. This is represented mathematically as: $| \Psi(t) \rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} (|e_i\rangle \langle s_i| + |e_i^\dagger\rangle \langle s_i^\dagger|) $ Where $e_i^\dagger$ is the creation operator for the entangled particle and $s_i^\dagger$ is the creation operator for the storage unit. The system utilizes a quantum entanglement network to manage the manipulation and measurement of entangled particles, enabling parallel access to the distributed memory. While practical implementation presents significant challenges, this research explores the potential of quantum information transfer and its application to distributed memory systems, offering a fundamentally new approach to data access optimization. The theoretical framework presented here provides a basis for future research and development in this area.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Algorithms for Graph Traversal and Search
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum walk algorithms to graph traversal and search problems. Classical algorithms often struggle with the computational complexity of traversing and searching large graphs, leading to significant time and resource limitations. Quantum walks, utilizing superposition and interference, offer a potential pathway to achieve exponential speedups. This work details the theoretical framework for applying quantum walks to graph problems, specifically focusing on traversal and search tasks. We present a generalized approach for mapping graph structures onto quantum walk systems and discuss the key mathematical formulations involved. The core of our investigation revolves around the construction of quantum walk operators that mimic the movement and interaction rules inherent in graph traversal. We analyze the evolution of the quantum walk state and derive expressions for the probability of reaching a specific node in the graph. Furthermore, we examine the impact of graph topology on the performance of the quantum walk, highlighting the potential for tailored algorithms to exploit specific graph structures. The results demonstrate the theoretical feasibility of quantum walk algorithms for significantly accelerating graph traversal and search operations, contributing to advancements in areas such as network analysis, database management, and artificial intelligence.

title: Title: Quantum Error Mitigation with Probabilistic Redundancy
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for groundbreaking technological advancements, but inherent quantum error rates pose a significant challenge to achieving fault-tolerant computations. Traditional error mitigation techniques, while effective, often involve complex and computationally intensive procedures. This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum error mitigation utilizing probabilistic redundancy, dynamically adjusting a noise profile to trigger redundant computations when errors are detected. This method aims to provide a more efficient and practical solution compared to existing approaches, offering a pathway towards achieving reliable results with reduced overhead. We detail the core mechanism, explore its theoretical implications, and present preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in mitigating errors.

title: Building Trustworthy Graph-Agentic RAG for Social Good: Architectures, Failure Propagation, and Assurance by Construction
abstract: Graph-agentic retrieval-augmented generation combines structured evidence with adaptive controllers that can plan retrieval, traverse relations, verify intermediate claims, delegate subtasks, and use tools. This combination is useful when answers depend on relations across documents, entities, time, or institutions, but it also creates coupled failure paths: a defect in graph construction can become retrieved evidence, alter later control decisions, and propagate toward a consequential outcome. We examine how such systems should be designed and evaluated for social-good settings in which freshness, authorization, traceability, oversight, and recourse matter alongside answer quality. We organize the literature by graph substrate, graph lifecycle, agent function, coordination pattern, and authority boundary, and distinguish graph-based retrieval from observation-dependent graph control. We then synthesize reported risks as an evidence-to-action failure chain and propose an assurance-by-construction blueprint comprising five interface contracts for evidence, retrieval, reasoning, capability and delegation, and outcome. These contracts make provenance, temporal validity, authorization, uncertainty, and recoverability explicit at system boundaries. An illustrative public-benefit information design shows how the framework constrains graph structure, permissions, abstention, and operating authority. Finally, we derive an evaluation agenda spanning graph assertions, trajectories, claims, coordination, and outcomes.

These contracts make provenance, temporal validity, authorization, uncertainty, and recoverability explicit at system boundaries. An illustrative public-benefit information design shows how the framework constrains graph structure, permissions, abstention, and operating authority. Finally, we derive an evaluation agenda spanning graph assertions, trajectories, claims, coordination, and outcomes.

title: Cogito, Ergo Prompt: Understanding how LLMs can Support Data Work
abstract: Large language models improve productivity in knowledge work, yet their outcome is contingent on the quality of the input prompt. While prompting is increasingly becoming a professional skill, prompt engineering guidance re- mains largely generic and detached from concrete work contexts. In this paper, we focus on data work, as an important yet understudied field of knowledge work. We systematically develop a configurable template that supports the crea- tion of task-specific prompts for data stewards. The evaluation of the prompts in naturalistic sessions involving 185 data professionals from around 40 organiza- tions indicates high perceived utility and efficiency of prompts with similar re- sults across tested models. The study contributes a configuragble template, as design science artifact, and transferable design knowledge for adapting prompt design to cognitively complex, tacit, and coordination-intensive tasks. It thereby lays the foundation for redesigning routines in knowledge work with LLMs sup- port.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Quantum Computing (DAQF)
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for unprecedented computational power, but its practical implementation faces significant challenges related to algorithm design, error correction, and computational resource management. This paper proposes a novel quantum computing framework, Dynamic Adaptive Quantum Computing (DAQF), designed to address these challenges by dynamically adjusting quantum computation parameters based on the inherent characteristics of the quantum process itself. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DAQF through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing its capacity to enhance both computational efficiency and accuracy compared to static parameter settings. The core mechanism of DAQF involves a feedback loop that continuously monitors the quantum state and adjusts parameters to optimize the algorithm's performance. This paper offers a new approach to quantum computing, promising significant advancements in the design and operation of quantum algorithms.

title: Geometric Quantum Computation Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric quantum computation framework designed to simulate and predict complex geometric shapes. Traditional computational methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of geometric data, requiring significant computational resources and time. This framework leverages quantum computation's unique capabilities – superposition, entanglement, and interference – to efficiently represent and manipulate geometric data, enabling novel modeling and analysis. We propose a layered architecture comprising a quantum state encoder, a geometric evolution simulator, and a readout mechanism, all underpinned by a sophisticated quantum algorithm for iterative refinement. The core mechanism centers around mapping geometric primitives into quantum states, facilitating rapid exploration of the space of possible shapes and their evolutions. The framework's design addresses challenges associated with geometric data representation and computation, offering the potential for significant advancements in areas like geometric modeling, simulations, and analysis.

title: ##混沌量子计算的自适应几何映射
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computation, leveraging the principles of chaos and geometry to enhance the computational capabilities of quantum systems. We introduce a method, termed "Adaptive Geometric Mapping," which dynamically adjusts the quantum state through a carefully designed mapping function, resulting in quantum states with predetermined geometric properties. This allows for the exploration of previously inaccessible quantum states and the development of novel quantum algorithms. The core claim is that this approach offers a significant advancement in quantum computation, enabling more effective quantum algorithms and expanding the range of solvable problems. This work explores the fundamental concepts of chaos and geometry, outlining the design and implementation of the Adaptive Geometric Mapping algorithm, highlighting its potential impact on the field of quantum information processing.

title: Title: Adaptive Metric Learning via Statistical Heterogeneity
abstract: Adaptive metric learning aims to improve model accuracy and robustness in complex datasets by dynamically adapting to the statistical heterogeneity of data distributions. This paper introduces a novel metric learning algorithm that learns a metric sensitive to local data point distributions, addressing the limitations of traditional approaches. We propose a framework that employs a novel attention mechanism to identify and leverage these local patterns, resulting in enhanced model performance across a range of datasets. The algorithm is designed to be robust to data drift and effectively handle complex, non-stationary distributions. We present experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of our approach in several challenging scenarios, highlighting its potential for advancing the field of metric learning.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a unique challenge and opportunity for information processing. This paper explores the development of a novel computational framework predicated on the intricate properties of quantum entanglement, aiming to leverage this non-classical interaction for enhanced information processing capabilities. The core claim is to establish a robust mathematical model of entangled states, utilizing the inherent non-classical characteristics of entanglement to design a computational paradigm. This approach seeks to overcome limitations inherent in current classical computational paradigms by directly exploiting the potential of entanglement. We delve into the conceptual foundations of this framework, outlining the key mathematical models and computational mechanisms designed to harness the essence of quantum entanglement. This investigation will demonstrate the potential for a paradigm shift in information processing, moving beyond classical approaches.

title: Decentralized Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation and Adaptive Exploration
abstract: Decentralized reinforcement learning (DRL) presents significant challenges in achieving efficient and robust learning, primarily stemming from slow convergence rates and inadequate exploration. This work addresses these limitations by introducing a novel decentralized DRL agent that synergistically integrates intrinsic motivation signals and an adaptive exploration strategy. The core idea is to leverage internal signals of interest (e.g., surprise, novelty) to guide exploration and simultaneously adjust the exploration-exploitation trade-off based on the agent's evolving internal state. This approach results in a more directed and efficient learning process, leading to improved performance across various decentralized environments. The presented framework offers a practical solution for overcoming the inherent difficulties of DRL, paving the way for more intelligent and adaptable autonomous systems. Mathematical formulations detail the key components of this system, including the intrinsic motivation term, the adaptive exploration policy, and the overall learning objective. The system is designed to be modular and readily adaptable to diverse decentralized scenarios.

title: Title: Adaptive Hierarchy of Computational Models
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for constructing computational models through an adaptive hierarchy of levels. The core concept revolves around creating a layered approach, where each model level represents a progressively more abstract and complex representation of the underlying phenomenon. The design incorporates a refined refinement process, where models are built up incrementally, leveraging information gained at each stage to enhance their predictive power and interpretability. This adaptive approach contrasts with traditional hierarchical models that often rely on static, predefined structures. We explore the fundamental principles behind this hierarchical design, detailing the mechanism for model construction, the benefits of this structure, and a preliminary assessment of its performance. This work contributes to the field of computational modeling by providing a robust and adaptable framework for developing models with enhanced complexity and interpretability. The system's adaptability will be demonstrated through illustrative examples across a simulated scenario.

title: Context-Aware Data Stream Summarization with Temporal Memory Networks
abstract: Data stream summarization is a critical task in various applications, ranging from real-time monitoring to anomaly detection. Traditional data stream summarization methods often struggle to effectively capture the temporal context inherent in streaming data, leading to summaries that lack crucial temporal insights. This paper proposes a novel approach that integrates Temporal Memory Networks (TMNs) with data stream summarization. TMNs, known for their ability to model and learn temporal dependencies, are leveraged to create a system capable of generating more accurate and informative summaries by explicitly considering the evolution of data streams over time. The system learns patterns and trends within the data stream and uses this knowledge to produce summaries that reflect the temporal dynamics. This work demonstrates the potential of TMNs for significantly improving the quality and usefulness of data stream summaries. The core claim of this research is that existing data stream summarization techniques frequently fail to account for the temporal context present in data streams. We introduce a system utilizing TMNs to model these temporal dependencies, resulting in summaries that accurately represent the data's evolution.

title: A Physics-Based Quantum Computing Compiler
abstract: This paper proposes and details the design of a novel quantum computing compiler, termed a Physics-Based Quantum Computing Compiler (PBQCC). The core innovation lies in automating the process of quantum algorithm generation by directly translating physical laws – specifically, quantum mechanical equations – into executable quantum circuits. Traditional quantum algorithm design relies heavily on manual coding, a process prone to human error and limited by the designer's expertise. The PBQCC utilizes a formal language and symbolic deduction to achieve this automation. The compiler takes a high-level description of a physical system and its desired manipulation (expressed within a physics-based framework) as input, and then generates an optimized quantum circuit that embodies the solution. This approach fundamentally shifts the paradigm from algorithm design to physics-driven computation, offering the potential for significantly increased efficiency, scalability, and accessibility within the quantum computing domain. The compiler incorporates optimization techniques and validation steps to ensure the fidelity and correctness of the generated quantum circuits. This document outlines the architecture, key components, and operational principles of the PBQCC, emphasizing its potential to revolutionize quantum algorithm development. ---

title: Information-Theoretic Analysis of Neural Network Training
abstract: This paper explores the application of information-theoretic principles to analyze and diagnose the training process of neural networks. Traditional methods for understanding neural network training often rely on empirical observations of loss and gradient magnitudes, which can be insufficient for capturing the subtle dynamics occurring within the network. We propose utilizing entropy and mutual information as key metrics to quantify information flow during training, offering a more granular and potentially insightful perspective. Specifically, we investigate how changes in entropy and mutual information between activations and gradients can reveal underlying issues such as vanishing gradients, mode collapse, and suboptimal learning rates. The core of our approach lies in establishing a diagnostic framework where these information-theoretic measures serve as indicators of training health. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis and conceptual discussion, the potential benefits of this approach and outline directions for future research, including the development of automated diagnostic tools based on these principles.

title: Supplementary Data for Small Language Models for AEC Tasks: Technology Evolution, Current Practices, and Future AI Systems
abstract: # Supplementary Data Package This package contains this README and four supplementary workbooks documenting the study corpus, screening validation, study-level reporting and evaluation characteristics, and the evidence summarized in manuscript Tables 5 and 6. `Supplementary_Table_S1_Corpus_and_Search.xlsx` documents the evidence base used in the review. Its `Corpus_132` worksheet lists the 132 included studies with bibliographic identifiers and task classifications, while `Seed_Reviews_22` records the 22 review-derived seed sources and their role in retrieval. The workbook supports the corpus construction, study identification, and task-classification information described in Section 3.1 and used throughout the evidence map. The seed set documents one retrieval route and is not treated as an independent recall-estimation sample. `Supplementary_Table_S2_Screening_Validation.xlsx` documents the screening-validation exercise. It reports agreement statistics for a 40-record sample, preserves the archived AI decisions and the scores and inclusion decisions of two independent reviewers, and defines the screening categories. The workbook supports the screening-validation procedure and agreement results reported in Section 3.1. The original blinded decisions remain separate from the later adjudication results. Supplementary Table S3 provides study-level reporting and evaluation-quality coding for all 132 included studies. It covers parameter disclosure, operational SLM eligibility, inference and deployment reporting, public availability of evaluation materials, baseline comparability, test-set size, run repetition, prompt disclosure, model or API version disclosure, and decoding settings. Definitions and page-labelled supporting evidence are retained in the same workbook. These data support the reporting statements that qualify the comparative synthesis, including the study counts reported at the beginning of Section 3.5 and the statements concerning public data, comparable baselines, test-set reporting, repeated runs, prompts, and model versions. `Supplementary_Table_S4_Table5_Table6_Evidence.xlsx` contains the evidence used for the two principal SLM syntheses. Its `Table5_Eligibility` worksheet lists 32 formal empirical SLM studies: 29 with a verified focal generative model below 10B and three admitted through an official mini designation whose parameter count was not disclosed. Its `Table6_Evidence` worksheet provides 29 task-level comparison records from 23 studies, including task class, evaluation standard, A0/A1/A2 adaptation profiles, P1/P2 models, selected results, and bounded interpretations. The first worksheet supports manuscript Table 5 and Section 3.4, whereas the second supports manuscript Table 6 and Section 3.5. Table 5 is the broader study-level inventory and does not require a larger-model comparator; Table 6 is its comparative task-level subset. The identifiers `AEC-001` to `AEC-132` are stable across the workbooks, and citation keys and DOIs link the records to the manuscript bibliography. `NA`, `unknown`, and related missingness codes are retained when a paper does not report a value or when a comparison is not applicable; unreported information is not imputed. The definitions included in each workbook govern the interpretation of its coded fields. The workbooks provide supporting evidence rather than replacing the manuscript tables: Table 5 identifies the 32-study SLM evidence base, Table 6 presents the 23-study comparison subset, and Supplementary Table S4 preserves study- and task-level traceability. Detailed screening and coding prompts described in the manuscript supplementary appendices are not duplicated in this data package.

The workbook supports the corpus construction, study identification, and task-classification information described in Section 3.1 and used throughout the evidence map. The seed set documents one retrieval route and is not treated as an independent recall-estimation sample. `Supplementary_Table_S2_Screening_Validation.xlsx` documents the screening-validation exercise. It reports agreement statistics for a 40-record sample, preserves the archived AI decisions and the scores and inclusion decisions of two independent reviewers, and defines the screening categories. The workbook supports the screening-validation procedure and agreement results reported in Section 3.1. The original blinded decisions remain separate from the later adjudication results. Supplementary Table S3 provides study-level reporting and evaluation-quality coding for all 132 included studies. It covers parameter disclosure, operational SLM eligibility, inference and deployment reporting, public availability of evaluation materials, baseline comparability, test-set size, run repetition, prompt disclosure, model or API version disclosure, and decoding settings. Definitions and page-labelled supporting evidence are retained in the same workbook. These data support the reporting statements that qualify the comparative synthesis, including the study counts reported at the beginning of Section 3.5 and the statements concerning public data, comparable baselines, test-set reporting, repeated runs, prompts, and model versions. `Supplementary_Table_S4_Table5_Table6_Evidence.xlsx` contains the evidence used for the two principal SLM syntheses. Its `Table5_Eligibility` worksheet lists 32 formal empirical SLM studies: 29 with a verified focal generative model below 10B and three admitted through an official mini designation whose parameter count was not disclosed. Its `Table6_Evidence` worksheet provides 29 task-level comparison records from 23 studies, including task class, evaluation standard, A0/A1/A2 adaptation profiles, P1/P2 models, selected results, and bounded interpretations. The first worksheet supports manuscript Table 5 and Section 3.4, whereas the second supports manuscript Table 6 and Section 3.5. Table 5 is the broader study-level inventory and does not require a larger-model comparator; Table 6 is its comparative task-level subset. The identifiers `AEC-001` to `AEC-132` are stable across the workbooks, and citation keys and DOIs link the records to the manuscript bibliography. `NA`, `unknown`, and related missingness codes are retained when a paper does not report a value or when a comparison is not applicable; unreported information is not imputed. The definitions included in each workbook govern the interpretation of its coded fields. The workbooks provide supporting evidence rather than replacing the manuscript tables: Table 5 identifies the 32-study SLM evidence base, Table 6 presents the 23-study comparison subset, and Supplementary Table S4 preserves study- and task-level traceability. Detailed screening and coding prompts described in the manuscript supplementary appendices are not duplicated in this data package.

title: CALM: A Calibrated LLM Choice Network Framework for Activity-Based Traveler Simulation
abstract: We present CALM, a reproducible hybrid framework that integrates an optional large language model (LLM) activity planner with calibrated stochastic choice, shared network feedback, memory and habit, typed feasibility checks, and deterministic offline replay. Unlike trip-mode classifiers or diary-only generators, CALM executes a closed traveler-day loop and evaluates each generative module against an empirical, reproducible baseline. On the 2024 New York City Citywide Mobility Survey (CMS), 110,691 seven-mode trips are split by respondent into 78,487 training and 32,204 holdout trips. Training-only alternative-specific constant calibration reduces mean holdout mode Jensen-Shannon divergence from 0.15599 to 0.00394 across ten seeds. A matched live-LLM ablation then quantifies trade-offs among aggregate fit, temporal fit, behavioral persistence, and feasibility, while frozen prompt-response pairs support deterministic replay of downstream simulation. Controlled weather, delay, fare, and parking ladders further demonstrate consistent and interpretable responses under intervention. CALM contributes a reproducible protocol for integrating and evaluating generative planners in traveler simulation through person-disjoint calibration, matched module ablation, controlled stress testing, and end-to-end traceability.

title: Contact order governs the onset of entanglement cascades
abstract: Entangling rates describe a direct entangling channel, but give no information when that channel is forbidden. For finite-dimensional analytic pure-state dynamics, we show that the onset of genuine $(n+1)$-partite entanglement is determined by the contact order $m_\star$ between the physical trajectory and the $S|E$ product manifold. It is the first Taylor order that cannot be reproduced by any product curve, or equivalently the first nonvanishing order of the Fubini--Study distance from the product manifold. We derive a time-ordered recursion that removes curvature-induced kinematic terms and computes $m_\star$ from the Taylor coefficients of $H(t)$. This provides a geometric description of an entanglement cascade, in which new subsystems can join multipartite entanglement only after one or more interaction steps. A symmetry-protected three-qubit model realizes $m_\star=2$, and a three-mode bosonic example shows that genuine tripartite entanglement can arise even when the two newly formed reduced pairs remain separable.

title: TD-STGT: A Spatio-Temporal Graph Transformer for Mobile Traffic Demand Forecasting
abstract: Fine-grained mobile traffic demand forecasting is essential for long-term planning of 5G and future 6G networks, including radio upgrades, site densification, backhaul expansion, and spectrum activation. This paper proposes the Traffic Demand Spatio-Temporal Graph Transformer (TD-STGT), a graph neural forecasting framework for predicting changes in wireless mobile traffic demand across fine geographic grids. The framework uses a population-scaled demand proxy developed from crowdsourced mobile measurements and daytime population information. Experiments across five Canadian metropolitan regions show that TD-STGT achieves the best performance in forecasting grid-level demand changes, reaching a $ΔR^2$ of 0.462 and reducing $Δ$RMSE by 5.7\% relative to the strongest baseline. The proposed model provides a practical tool for identifying areas with increasing demand pressure and prioritizing future mobile-network capacity upgrades.

title: Event Interaction in Low-Rank Bottlenecks for Temporal Relation Extraction
abstract: Temporal relation extraction determines whether an event occurs before, after, or simultaneously with another event, and therefore relies on accurately modeling how the two events interact. Mainstream systems achieve this by concatenating event spans or using shallow fusion, which works well when all model parameters are trainable. However, in parameter-efficient fine-tuning, low-rank bottlenecks restrict information flow and prevent these interaction signals from passing through, leading to clear performance drops. To address this limitation, we propose a theoretically grounded architecture, Convolutional Bottleneck Interaction (CBI), which first applies lightweight depthwise convolution to enhance event representations and then uses element-wise multiplication to capture effective event-event interactions inside the bottleneck. Across five datasets and seven backbone models in the Adapter and LoRA settings, CBI provides consistent and substantial gains, up to +31.7 micro F1, while adding minimal computational cost, showing that explicit interaction inside low-rank spaces is crucial for temporal relation extraction. The code is available at https://github.com/VRCMF/CIF.git.

title: ChromSep Tutor Critique — Registered Session Transcripts (2026-09-06)
abstract: Six session transcripts collected as the primary evidence underlying Table 1 of "Critique: ChromSep Tutor — An LLM-Based Tutoring System Coupled to a Validated Preparative Chromatography Simulator via the Model Context Protocol (MCP)" (David P. R. Moreno, L. H. Reyes, J. C. Cruz Jiménez, Universidad de los Andes). All six sessions were conducted on September 6, 2026, with ChromSep Tutor (LUT University), an LLM-based tutoring system coupled to the multicol24 preparative chromatography simulator. The sessions cross the three curriculum modes offered by the tool — Chromatography Fundamentals, Chromatography Process Design, and Free Exploration — with two models available through the interface: Claude Opus (reasoning effort: medium) and DeepSeek-V4-Pro (reasoning effort: high). Transcripts were captured manually, in real time, by copying the conversation text before closing the interface, since the tool provides no session export or persistence across a page reload. Sessions were conducted in Spanish. Files: FUND-OPUS.txt — Chromatography Fundamentals, Claude Opus, 20 turns FUND-DEEPSEEK.txt — Chromatography Fundamentals, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 20 turns PROCESS-OPUS.txt — Chromatography Process Design, Claude Opus, 18 turns PROCESS-DEEPSEEK.txt — Chromatography Process Design, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 25 turns FREE-OPUS.txt — Free Exploration, Claude Opus, 9 turns FREE-DEEPSEEK.txt — Free Exploration, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, 6 turns Three additional sessions, one per module, were run beforehand solely to familiarize the authors with the interface. Because the interface does not persist sessions across a page reload and offers no export function, these familiarization sessions were not transcribed with sufficient fidelity to serve as evidence and are not included in this dataset.

title: The Agreement Walk Calculus: A Federated Formalization in Lean, Coq, and Agda
abstract: Initial public release of the Agreement Walk Calculus — three independent proof-kernel formalizations of a position assistant. Contents Lean 4 (lean/): Full formalization with AgreementWalk.lean and ProofKernel.lean Coq (coq/): Independent formalization with AgreementWalk.v and ProofKernel.v Agda (agda/): Independent formalization with AgreementWalk.agda and ProofKernel.agda Each kernel proves the same three theorems: Walk well-formedness (every step is a valid transition) Agreement preservation (agreement holds at every step) Termination (every walk reaches a terminal state) Verification All three proof kernels type-check independently. title: 基于自适应的循环神经网络的参数调整策略
abstract: This paper presents a novel parameter adjustment strategy for recurrent neural networks (RNNs) based on adaptive algorithms. Traditional parameter tuning methods often involve manual adjustments, which can be inefficient and lack adaptability. This work introduces a dynamic adjustment process that automatically adjusts network structure based on training data characteristics, leading to enhanced feature extraction performance. The core mechanism utilizes an iterative refinement loop, continuously optimizing the network's architecture to maximize information gain. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, showcasing improved accuracy and efficiency compared to existing parameter tuning techniques. This research addresses the limitations of traditional methods and offers a promising pathway toward more robust and automated RNN design.

title: Master Equation River — Coq formalisation of every equation (v1.0: equations 1–79 of Master Equation River v1.4)
abstract: What this is. A Coq 8.20 development (readout-first, finite/discrete models only: nat, Z, Q, bool, finite lists and records; no Coq.Reals, no classical axioms, no Admitted, no top-level Axiom/Parameter) that formalises every numbered equation of Master Equation River v1.4 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22414412, concept), equations 1–79. Each equation is placed at exactly one tier: Th_coqc where a statement is derivable in a stated finite model (non-collapse laws proved by exhibiting a finite model in which the two readouts differ; accounting identities such as the Citizen Claim Threshold; nesting Πlive ⊆ Πfeas ⊆ Πphys; the discrete-difference form of the audit-index identity; Ẏ>0 ⇏ ṖH>0; Machine expansion ⇏ Human expansion), Definition where the paper defines an object (state spaces, readout maps, vectors, the river as a typed composition), and Open where the paper marks a hypothesis open (stated as a Prop, never proved). verify.sh runs Print Assumptions on every lemma; all report Closed under the global context. MR_Ledger.md maps equation → module → identifier → tier → assumptions, and records where a proved lemma is only a narrow witness of a thesis the paper itself keeps at tier Dr (equations 5, 8, 16). Continuum-looking expressions in the paper (exp, ∂ ln, max over infinite sets) are replaced by declared discrete counterparts and the replacement is recorded in the source comments. Status. K0 working release of the programme; the formalisation checks internal consistency of the stated discrete models, not empirical truth. Founder ruling BBL-2026-09-06-165 (Blackbox Log). An AI assistant drafted the modules under the author's direction; no AI system is an author or contributor.

title: Quantum State Information Matching
abstract: Quantum State Information Matching is a novel approach to quantum information matching that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to establish a robust and efficient correspondence between different quantum states. This paper presents a new algorithm predicated on the principle of quantum state information matching, utilizing entanglement to create a bridge between states, facilitating precise and reliable matching without relying on conventional statistical methods. The core mechanism centers around the generation of entangled states, facilitating the correlation and comparison of states, thereby enabling the detection of subtle differences and the establishment of a complete correspondence. The algorithm's potential impact spans across various quantum computing applications, offering a more accurate and dependable method for managing and interpreting quantum information.

title: Dimension Mapping Algorithm - Dynamic Space Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Dimension Mapping Algorithm (DMA) that leverages deep neural networks to dynamically adjust the dimensionality of a space, optimizing linear algebra and quantum computation, particularly in the context of high-dimensional polynomial equations and quantum states. Traditional methods rely on static parameter adjustments, while NAS and graph-based representation learning offer a flexible and adaptive approach. The DMA's core mechanism centers around a self-adaptive neural network (NAS) that continuously learns and adjusts the dimensionality of the space, leading to significant efficiency gains. This research addresses the limitations of existing methods, specifically focusing on handling complex equations and quantum states, and offers a promising solution for enhanced computational performance.

title: Quantum Geometry Error Correction Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum computing's unique properties to develop a novel error correction strategy for quantum computation. Specifically, we propose a quantum geometry error correction approach that transforms geometric calculations into quantum state correction, aiming to mitigate the inherent geometric errors that plague current quantum algorithms. We detail the core mechanisms involved, including the incorporation of quantum entanglement and error-correcting protocols. The paper highlights the significance of this approach for improving the reliability of quantum algorithms, particularly in applications requiring high-precision geometric operations. The investigation begins with a conceptual overview of the challenges associated with geometric error correction and concludes with a discussion of the potential benefits and limitations of this new method.

title: Adaptive Quantum System Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum system modeling framework leveraging quantum mechanics and machine learning to construct more accurate quantum system models. The core mechanism centers on dynamically adjusting the model based on the system's state, leading to improved quantum computing efficiency. This approach addresses limitations of traditional models, which rely on static parameters, and offers a novel methodology for enhanced quantum simulation capabilities. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the framework's effectiveness in modeling a specific quantum system, highlighting its potential for accelerating quantum algorithm development.

title: Quantum Entanglement Geometry Transformation and Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to geometry optimization. We propose a novel algorithm, termed "Quantum Entanglement Geometry Transformation," that leverages the unique properties of entangled states to perform geometric transformations. The core mechanism hinges on manipulating the entangled state space to achieve optimized geometric results. The research explores the potential of this approach to surpass traditional geometric optimization techniques, particularly in scenarios involving complex and highly interconnected geometric structures. The paper details the algorithm's design, the mathematical framework underpinning its operation, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness. The investigation considers the role of entanglement in the algorithm's optimization process and its potential impact on the resulting geometric structures.

title: Self-Correcting Programming Languages via Formal Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to programming language design centered around self-correction capabilities achieved through the integration of formal verification techniques. The core idea is to construct programming languages where errors are not merely detected at runtime or compile-time, but proactively identified and corrected during the compilation process itself. This is accomplished by embedding a formal verification engine directly into the language's compilation pipeline, leveraging methodologies like model checking to rigorously validate program code against formally specified properties. The resulting languages would fundamentally shift the paradigm from reactive error handling to proactive error prevention, potentially leading to significantly more reliable and robust software systems. This research explores the architectural considerations, formal methods, and challenges associated with realizing such a system, arguing for a significant advancement in software development practices. The paper focuses on the theoretical foundations and outlines a roadmap for future exploration within this domain.
